messages:
sara: Heads-up — Acme Health asked for guidance on how big their Redwood Dedicated commit should be. They want predictable throughput for two models: chat-micro (short convo, ~40 tok/resp) and embed-lite (256-dim). They gave expected 95th pct concurrency: 180 chat reqs/min and 450 embed reqs/min. Can we translate to GPU commit sizing and a ballpark monthly commit cost? :thinking:

ton y: Quick approach: convert to tokens/sec sustained then divide by profiled GPU tokens/sec for each model+GPU type. Use p95 workload, not mean. Example calc: 

```
# chat
chat_tpm = 180 req/min
avg_tokens = 40
chat_tokens_per_sec = (chat_tpm * avg_tokens) / 60
# if A10G @ batch=8 -> ~220 tokens/sec (profiled)
needed_gpus = ceil(chat_tokens_per_sec / 220)
```

For embed-lite we use vector throughput (embeds/sec). A10G can do ~1200 small-embeds/min (~20 embeds/sec) depending on preprocessing. So do per-model and sum the GPU slots.

ton y: Plugging numbers quickly: chat_tokens_per_sec = (180*40)/60 = 120 tps -> 120/220 = 0.55 -> 1 A10G for chat headroom. embed: 450/60 = 7.5 req/s -> 7.5/20 = 0.375 -> 1 A10G if colocated but because of isolation and peaks we recommend 2 A10G total (1 primary + 1 buffer) -> gives room for spikes and rolling replace. :+1:

mahima: Note on contracts — our Dedicated commits are sold as reserved GPU-hours per month (or equivalent committed vGPU slots). Recommend sizing to ~1.6x observed p95 to cover growth and burst policy, or offer "commit + burst credits" model. Also FYI: eu-west-1 had spot interruption-induced billing anomalies last month — if we seat customer in eu-west, prefer reserved pricing rather than burst-on-demand heavy usage. :warning:

carl: From FinOps POV, if we commit 2 A10Gs in-region reserved, ballpark cloud cost (committed) is $26k/mo after discounts; on-demand for same baseline traffic w/ 20% buffer was ~ $48k/mo during our sim. That's a material delta — mention this to the customer with clear notes about burst and SLA. We should prepare a 12-month vs 3-month pricing option.

infra-bot: [metric] dedicated-pool-acme-health usage snapshot: reserved_pool_utilization=68% at 14:02 UTC, rolling_p95_latency=190ms (chat-micro), embed-p50=120ms. Scheduled maintenance window 03/12 02:00-03:00 UTC.

kevin: Suggest run a 14-day canary with a 60% commit (1 A10G) and allow burst to on-demand for the rest. Measure real tokens/sec distribution and cold-start tail. Proposed experiment steps: 
```
1) create capacity-profile acme-canary (commit=1 A10G, burst_limit=1 A10G)
2) route 25% prod traffic -> acme-canary over 14d
3) collect per-model token/sec histograms, p95 latency, and cloud cost attribution tags
```

finops: Quick billing caveat — we spotted a tagging mismatch last quarter where embed jobs came through unlabeled and were billed to infra pool; we need customer-specific resource tags on the dedicated pool before canary to ensure accurate chargeback. I'll open the cloud ticket to backfill missing tags. :memo:

mahima: Also think about GPU family: A10G is cost-effective for short-chat and embeds, but if customer later runs long context Llama-2-70B we should plan for A100 or H100 variant sizing and a migration plan. Include model-variant cost table in the proposal.

tony: One more: take the 99th percentile of request size (not just p95 req/min). We had an incident where batched long responses pushed a single GPU over token/sec and caused p99 latency spikes. For proposals use conservative multiplex factor (0.7 effective throughput) when converting theoretical tokens/sec to committed GPUs.

sara: Action items: (1) Tony to produce a short calc spreadsheet with the formulas and conservative multipliers; (2) Kevin to draft the 14-day canary runbook + infra config snippet; (3) Finops/Carl to prepare commit vs on-demand cost table (3/12/12 mo); (4) Mahima to add region risk note (eu-west preemption) and recommend GPU family options. I'll assemble the customer proposal after those and propose 2 A10G reserved commit with the canary. :eyes:
